item: Each import report says why its article conflicts happened and which engines stamped the backup
summary: An article conflict is two rows with the same content hash (SHA-256 of the body with whitespace collapsed) and different stored bytes. The report now splits them into whitespace_only (same text laid out differently), local_changed, incoming_changed and both_changed (that side no longer hashes to its stored hash: rewritten after it was stored), under _article_conflicts. The derived-row carry plan lists the backup's own engine stamps with their article counts (incoming_engines, incoming_www_engines), so a carry that matched nothing names what it saw. The conflict sample is taken in the same pass, which removes a second join that on a backup with few conflicts read every matched pair's text again. Totals, the local-kept rule and additivity are unchanged.
